messages:
Maya (Docs): Hey team, quick coordination thread for a couple small but important model-catalog updates: seq_len limits for quantized Mistral variants, an SDK snippet migration, and a broken benchmark link. I opened two tiny PRs: #5021 (catalog limits + compat note) and #5022 (docs snippets + links).

Jon (ML Eng): Thanks — saw #5021. The seq_len numbers we published were conservative for fp16 but too low for 8-bit quant. For mistral-7b-8q we can allow 2048 in our benchmarks; we should call out that latency increases ~15% after 1024 tokens. Add a compatibility note about KV-cache memory behavior for 8-bit kernels.

Maya (Docs): Copy. Can you paste the exact wording you want for the compatibility note? I want to avoid accidentally implying it's an accuracy regression.

Jon (ML Eng): Sure: "Note: Quantized variants use an 8-bit kernel that may increase KV-cache memory usage and per-token latency for very long sequences. We observed ~15% higher latency >1024 tokens vs fp16 in our benchmark harness; quality (perplexity) is not impacted in our tests." Keep it short.

Alex (SDK): I can update the snippet in #5022. FYI there was also an old example that uses the legacy generate() call — we should migrate examples to responses.create + streaming example. Current old snippet in docs: 

```python
# old example (do not use)
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=...)
resp = client.generate(model="mistral-7b", prompt="Summarize this...", max_tokens=150)
print(resp.text)
```

New SDK pattern we should show: 

```python
# new example (responses API)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${API_KEY}")
with client.responses.stream(model="mistral-7b-8q") as stream:
    stream.send("Summarize this article in 3 bullets")
    for chunk in stream.iter_text():
        print(chunk, end="")
```

Alex (SDK): I'll push the snippet change and add a short migration note: "If you previously used client.generate(...) switch to client.responses.create(...) or client.responses.stream(...) for streaming output."

Tess (Product): Please also add a tiny note in the catalog card about supported deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated) for quantized models. Ops teams keep asking whether 8q is supported on Dedicated.

Maya (Docs): Good call. Jon, can you confirm Dedicated is supported but requires the quant kernel flag in runtime (runtime-config: quant_kernels: "avx2" / "cuda-..." or similar)? I can paraphrase for the card.

Jon (ML Eng): Confirmed: Dedicated supports 8q; operator needs the quant kernel flag on the node pool. Suggest text: "Dedicated: supported (requires enabling quant kernels in runtime config)."

Chris (Benchmarks): Also noticed the benchmark sheet link in the model card points to an old sheet (404). Created a new public sheet and put the latest run results at https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1A_sample_bench (please replace with canonical link in PR). The new sheet includes seq_len sweep data and the latency delta table referenced above.

Maya (Docs): Great — I'll swap the link in #5022. Alex, after you update the snippet can you also add a tiny note under the code block linking to the benchmark sheet and to the runtime-compatibility paragraph?

Alex (SDK): Yep. Plan: push commit to #5022 with (a) new snippet, (b) migration text, (c) updated link. Will request review from @Maya and @Tess.

Maya (Docs): Thanks — schedule: aiming to merge both PRs today. If we merge, we should run a quick docs deploy to staging and sanity-check the rendered model card and snippet. deploy-bot, can you trigger a staging deploy when both PRs merge?

deploy-bot: noted. I will queue a staging deploy after both PRs are merged to main.

Tess (Product): Quick nit: in the catalog JSON we also have a "max_sequence_length" field used by the Console to show limits. Make sure PR #5021 updates that field for the 8q variant; otherwise Console will still ban inputs >1024.

Maya (Docs): Good catch. Jon, can you update the model catalog JSON in #5021 to bump max_sequence_length to 2048 for mistral-7b-8q and add a compatibility_tags array entry: ["quant-8bit","kv-cache-note"]. If you want I can run a tiny script to validate JSON after your change.

Jon (ML Eng): Done in branch. Included the compatibility tag and updated max_sequence_length. Pushed to #5021.

Alex (SDK): #5022 updated with snippet + migration blurb + link to Chris's sheet. PTAL.

Maya (Docs): Reviewing now. Quick checklist before merge: (1) PRs include changelog entries? (2) Console/JSON validated? (3) Bench link uses canonical published URL? (4) Snippet uses RedwoodClient naming and streaming example?

Alex (SDK): (1) yes, small changelog; (2) running validator, should pass; (3) link uses Chris's canonical URL; (4) yes streaming example uses RedwoodClient.

Maya (Docs): Okay I'm happy to merge once validator passes. @Tess if you can give final product ack I'll merge both and ping deploy-bot.

Tess (Product): ACK from product. :thumbsup:

Maya (Docs): Merged both. deploy-bot, please run staging deploy now.

deploy-bot: staging deploy queued — starting build. Logs: https://ci.internal/builds/7890

Chris (Benchmarks): Quick follow-up: I added one row to the sheet highlighting the 1024/2048 thresholds and the test commands to reproduce locally: `python -m bench_runner --model mistral-7b-8q --seq-len 2048`. Put that in the docs footnote if you like.

Maya (Docs): Adding footnote with the reproduce command and link to the sheet. Thanks everyone, nice small win.

Jon (ML Eng): :partyparrot:

Alex (SDK): Thanks y'all.

Tess (Product): Great work.
